pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:161 a per-document extraction failure is only warn-logged and :169 then finalizes the run 'completed' with error None, so a run where every document failed reads as a clean run that found 0 entities (extraction-failed spelled as empty); rows also bypass any domain door (:314 entityType never checked against the approved schema, :307 absent confidence becomes 1.0)

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:307 absent confidence is filled with 1.0, the maximum legal value, and :314 entity_type is inserted unchecked although the prompt says it 'must be one of the schema types' - shape-only serde door, no domain check; the one retry (src-tauri/engine/src/cli_process.rs:624) re-sends the unchanged prompt (kb_extract.rs:200) on a stronger model rather than feeding back path-addressed errors, though it is bounded and its exhaustion is a typed AppError::Validation

src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:230 the only rung is extract_fenced_block; there is no whole-text parse, balanced-span or tolerant-repair rung, so a clean unfenced JSON reply is rejected and spends the escalation call

src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:161 per-document failures exist only as a tracing::warn line; the run row records entity_count alone, with no failed-document count or failure category, so a drift from 2% to 50% failures is invisible on the surface

src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/vector_kb.rs:1255 the run is spawned with its handle discarded; the Err path at :1261 writes 'failed' to the row but emits no terminal progress event (only kb_extract.rs:169's completed path does), and a panic leaves the row 'running' forever

src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:187 the extraction request is open-ended ('one object per real instance you find'), not an enumerated set of units, so an empty row list is a legitimate outcome per document

pairs.registryProposal: schema-validation-and-repair could name 'escalate the identical prompt to a stronger model' as a distinct, weaker cousin of the error-fed repair loop: bounded and honest on exhaustion, but it spends a model turn without telling the producer what failed, and a reader can easily mistake it for the sanctioned repair loop.
